 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04-01-2023 at about 8.10 a.m., the petitioner was crossing the road as a pedestrian, near New Horizen College, Kadubisanahalli, Bengaluru.
At that time, the driver of Omni car bearing No.KA-04-N-1778, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering the human life and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Jeevika Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as an employee in private firm at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Hal Airport Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Omni Car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Omni car bearing No.KA-04-N-1778 and its liability, subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy and provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act and valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the omni car, as on the date Gopal Kumar vs Abdul Rahim T.S on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169156112/

Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, by knowingfully well that his driver T.S. Abdul Rahim S/o Saidu T.M., did not possess valid licence to drive the insured car at the time of accident.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.1 alone is liable to pay the entire compensation.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident the petitioner was crossing the road unmindfully, from the place where there are no zebra crossing marks and without observing the traffic on the said road, which has resulted in inevitable accident.
No actionable negligence can be attributed against the driver of the Omni car bearing No.KA-04-N-1778.
Further it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 9. Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 04-01-2023 at about 8.10 a.m., when the petitioner was crossing the road as a pedestrian, near New Horizen College, Kadubisanahalli,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of offending Omni car bearing No.KA-04-N-1778 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as an employee in private firm at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report,
Ex.P.7 is discharge summary, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is notarized copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.10 are medical bills, Ex.P.11 is OPD slip and Ex.P.12 is x- ray.

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6 and 8,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 and dashing the same to the petitioner, who was crossing the said road as a pedestrian.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries on his right leg and other parts of the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-N- 1778.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-N-1778 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner himself, who was crossing the road unmindfully, without observing the traffic on the said road and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778.

But,
the respondent No.2 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Administrative Officer of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car Gopal Kumar vs Abdul Rahim T.S on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169156112/
4 bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 and dashing the same the petitioner, while he was crossing the road as a pedestrian, near New Horizon College,
Kadubisanahalli, Bengaluru.
Further it reveals that, in the said accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his right leg.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to negligence of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
But, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, at the time of accident there was heavy traffic and movement of vehicles on the said road.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, nowhere in the petition or in the examination-in-chief affidavit the petitioner has stated that, at the place of accident there were zebra cross marks or provision for the pedestrians to cross the road.

Even, nowhere in the entire police investigation records it is stated that, at the place of accident there were zebra cross marks or there was provision for the pedestrian to cross the road from the said place.

This clearly goes to show that, the petitioner was crossing the road from the place were there was no provision for the pedestrians to cross the road, at the time when there was heavy movement of vehicles on the said road and the said negligent act of the petitioner has resulted in the accident.

If the petitioner had not attempted to cross the road from the place where there was no provision for the pedestrians to cross the road, the said accident would not have occurred and he would not have sustained injuries.

On the other hand, if the driver of offending Omni car had been diligent and taken necessary care while driving his vehicle and if he had driven his car slowly or in a moderate speed, he could have avoided the said accident.
Further, the driver of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and to observe traffic rules & regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that,
the accident in question has taken place due to contributory negligence of the petitioner as well as the driver of offending car.

But, as the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of offending car is more, this Court is of the further opinion that, holding the petitioner liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 20% and the driver of offending car at 80% in the cause of accident,
would be justified and it will meet the ends of justice.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of 40 feet wide on Kadubisanahalli- Doddakannahalli road, near New Horizen College, Kadubisanahalli, Bengaluru, due to dashing of offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-N-1778 to the petitioner, who was crossing the said road as a pedestrian.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.8 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said Gopal Kumar vs Abdul Rahim T.S on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169156112/
5 accident.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
Ex.P.11 OPD slip and Ex.P.12 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has suffered fractures of both bones (Tibia and Fibula) of right leg.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 04-01-2023 at about 8:10 a.m., on Kadubisanahalli-Doddakannahalli road, near New Horizen College, Kadubisanahalli,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-N-1778.
But, he has failed to prove that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Omni car.
For the reasons stated supra, this Court is come to conclusion that, there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner to the extent of 20% in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent Gopal Kumar vs Abdul Rahim T.S on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169156112/

sentences.text: The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fractures of both bones (Tibia and Fibula) of right leg and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning,
future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the petitioner is 04-03-1985.
The accident has taken place on 04-01-2023 at about 8:10 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 38 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fractures of both bones (tibia and Fibula) of right leg.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, there is 32.85% physical disability to right lower limb and 16.42% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.3 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary, Ex.P.11 OPD slip and Ex.P.12 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further,
he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 04-01-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 31-07- 2024, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, he has not treated the petitioner at any point of time and except wound certificate and discharge summary he has not verified any medical records of the petitioner.
Further he has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, fracture of Tibia of right leg is united and there is partial union of fracture of Fibula of right leg.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 14% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 14% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.

sentences.text: The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as an employee in private firm at Bengaluru and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as an employee in private firm, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2023.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.16,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner at Rs.1,92,000/-.

sentences.text: 31. Liability: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N- 1778.
As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy bearing No.0704053122P101093912, issued by the respondent No.2, in respect of offending Omni Car bearing No.KA-04-N- 1778, was valid from 05-05-2022 to 04-05-2023.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 04-01- 2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
32.

But, the respondent No.2 has taken specific defence that, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1/driver- cum-owner of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N- 1778 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
As there is breach of fundamental condition of the policy by the insured, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.1.

But, the witness examined by the respondent No.1 as R.W.2, who is none other than the Investigation Officer/Police Sub-Inspector who has conducted the investigation in the case and foisted charge-sheet against the accused, has himself clearly deposed in his evidence that, at the time of accident the respondent No.1/driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-04-N-1778 was holding valid learner's licence and in the said car one Mohammed Asim was sitting beside him, who was holding valid driving licence to drive the car.
This clearly establishes that, there was no breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,57,114/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
33. Issue No.3: In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,57,114/- (Rupees five lakh fifty seven thousand one hundred and fourteen only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Hal Airport Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Omni Car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 04-01-2023 at about 8.10 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-N-1778 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 04-01-2023 at about 8:10 a.m., on Kadubisanahalli-Doddakannahalli road, near New Horizen College, Kadubisanahalli,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-N-1778.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner himself, who was crossing the road unmindfully, without observing the traffic on the said road and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778.
Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is the representative/Administrative Officer of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car Gopal Kumar vs Abdul Rahim T.S on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169156112/
4 bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778.
On the other hand, if the driver of offending Omni car had been diligent and taken necessary care while driving his vehicle and if he had driven his car slowly or in a moderate speed, he could have avoided the said accident.
Further, the driver of a vehicle using public road is having higher duty to exercise reasonable care and to observe traffic rules & regulations, including yielding to pedestrians.
Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that,
the accident in question has taken place due to contributory negligence of the petitioner as well as the driver of offending car.
But, as the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of offending car is more, this Court is of the further opinion that, holding the petitioner liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 20% and the driver of offending car at 80% in the cause of accident,
would be justified and it will meet the ends of justice.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.8 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said Gopal Kumar vs Abdul Rahim T.S on 4 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169156112/
5 accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-N-1778 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 14% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 14% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
